title: The expression level of microRNA in invasive and noninvasive gonadotroph pituitary tumors
author: Bujko, Mateusz
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Assess RNA quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the small‑RNA fraction using an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with the Small RNA Kit Chip (Agilent) and quantify RNA with a Qubit RNA HS Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Construct sequencing library
steps.instruction: Prepare the library from 1 µg total RNA using the Ion Total RNA‑Seq Kit v2 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

substeps.instruction: Hybridize and ligate RNA adapters with the Ion Xpress™ RNA‑Seq Barcode Kit for multiplexing.
Perform reverse transcription, then purify cDNA and select library size using Nucleic Acid Binding Beads.
PCR‑amplify the cDNA, followed by DNA purification and a second size‑selection step.

steps.title: Verify library size and concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the amount and size distribution of the amplified DNA on a Bioanalyzer 2100 using the High Sensitivity DNA Kit (Agilent); confirm that miRNA ligation products in the barcoded libraries are 94–114 bp long.

steps.title: Prepare template for clonal amplification
steps.instruction: Dilute each library to 18 pM, pool up to four miRNA libraries, and load them onto a PI chip using the Ion Chef Instrument with the Ion PI™ Hi‑Q™ Chef Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Run the prepared PI chip on an Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to generate sequencing data.

steps.title: Convert BAM to FASTQ
steps.instruction: Convert unmapped BAM files to FASTQ format using the bamToFastq script from the bedtools suite.

steps.title: Map reads and quantify miRNAs
steps.instruction: Map reads to known human miRNAs (miRBase v.22) and quantify them using miRDeep2.14.

steps.title: Normalize read counts
steps.instruction: Perform data normalization of the miRNA read counts with DESeq2.
